summary: The statement and proof are mathematically correct as written. The Reis--Rothvoss theorem is invoked on exactly the positive-volume compact convex levels where its full-dimensional convex-body hypothesis holds; its eligible projected subspaces and determinant normalization match the candidate definitions. Translating a fixed level by one of its points preserves the covering predicate at each scale and yields nested dilates, so noncovering at scale one indeed forces covering radius greater than one. The quotient-lattice determinant identity, countability and measurability arguments, rank monotonicity, application of the accepted weighted sectional budget with W=B, nonatomic endpoint selection, treatment of lower-dimensional levels, constants, and the deliberately limited synchronized-certificate conclusion all check out.
